title: Pin governor: controlled fallback windows and variant throttling for pinned model versions
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers who pin model versions require guarantees that pinned traffic will not be silently rerouted to incompatible variants during regional capacity events or enforced deprecations. Current fallback behavior is coarse: it either allows a global automatic substitution (risking API surface regressions) or rejects traffic (customer-visible errors).

Goal: Implement a 'pin governor' policy that enables controlled, observable fallback windows with variant throttling and staged deprecation escalation. The governor should: (1) prefer same-version variants in other regions when compatible, (2) apply per-variant throttles (traffic shaping) during capacity shortfalls, (3) expose a grace/deprecation timeline with telemetry and auto-notifications, and (4) publish performance profiles so substitution decisions respect latency/cost SLO tradeoffs.

Scope: design + runtime implementation + console UX for policy configuration + telemetry dashboards + rollout plan. Not in scope: new quantization formats or model conversion tooling (those are separate onboarding tasks).
acceptance_criteria: Pinned endpoint will not return 5xx due to immediate global substitution for 95% of simulated regional outages; instead traffic will be throttled or routed with a visible fallback reason.
Operators can configure a per-pin 'fallback window' (0-72 hours) and an optional 'variant throttle' (0-100%) via API and Console.

Performance profile publishing: for any candidate variant, runtime picks substitution only if published profile meets the pinned version's latency/quality thresholds or is explicitly allowed by policy.
Telemetry dashboard shows per-pin fallback events, % traffic diverted, average token latency delta, and estimated cost delta within 5% of actual charges for test load.
Security review signoff completed (KMS/metadata handling for pin reasons and audit logs).
Integration tests that simulate: regional AZ failure, variant mismatch, and deprecation TTL expire, all passing in CI with deterministic assertions.
tasks: Design doc for pin governor and policy schema (Confluence)
Runtime: implement policy evaluator and per-variant token-level throttler
Routing: update smart router to prefer compatible same-version variants and respect throttle hints
Console: add pin policy UI and validation
Telemetry: dashboard + alert rules + structured fallback events to logging stream
E2E tests and chaos sims (regional isolation, warmup behavior)
Gradual rollout plan and canary with 5 internal customers
